chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Abu Dawud, altogether from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah), so he stood in the rain until it flowed over his body: 'Would that suffice him from the ghusl?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body washing

ai.seo_question: Is standing in the rain sufficient for ghusl if one is in a state of janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of ease (taysir) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating that the essential requirement for ghusl is the flow of water over the entire body, rather than a specific method of application. It serves as a practical precedent for using natural water sources like rain, reinforcing the validity of ghusl al-tamam (complete washing) when conditions permit. This ruling is particularly significant for travelers or those in arid regions, emphasizing the functional aspect of purification over ritual rigidity.
